title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC inherent corruption vs immediate extra us tip
pass_a_gloss: Next: if GAR holds Adam's own sin likewise ours only by imputation, how does that explain Christ/Adam difference—and if not, he contradicts what he has driven home several times. Further, if something inherent already deserts condemnation, why, not content with that desert, demand another sin placed outside us immediately imputed? You will say: to cause that internal vice we would otherwise lack. Then God freely, without necessity, imputes an outside sin so that by its force inner sin is produced—delighting in that internal evil. Is that to glorify God, or rather to make Him (spoken with horror of conscience) author of our sin?
pass_b_english: Next, to what end does he observe here that Christ's own righteousness is ours only by imputation, if he holds the same of the sin that is Adam's own—that it likewise is ours only by imputation? What does that do to explain the difference between Christ and Adam? Or if he does not hold that, he contradicts himself, seeing he has driven it home several times. Further, if there is something internal and inherent in us by whose desert we lie under condemnation, why, not content with that desert and that condemnation, do we want another sin placed outside us to be immediately imputed? You will say: that it may be the cause of this internal thing, which otherwise we would lack. God then delights in this internal sin, seeing that without any necessity He freely imputes to us that sin placed outside us, so that by the force of that imputation that internal sin may be produced in us which otherwise could not be produced. Is this to glorify God, and not rather to make Him (which I cannot pronounce without horror of conscience) the author of our sin?
source_text: Deinde quorsum observat hoc loco, justitiam Christi propriam, non esse nostram nisi imputatione, si idem censet de peccato quod Adami est proprium, id similiter non esse nostrum nisi imputatione? Quid enim hoc facit ad discrimen inter Christum & Adamum explicandum? Quod si id non censet, sibi ipse contradicit, quippe qui id aliquoties inculcavit. Praeterea, si est aliquid in nobis internum & inhaerens cujus merito condemnationi subjacemus, cur eo merito eaque condemnatione non contenti, volumus aliud peccatum extra nos positum immediate imputari? Nempe, inquies, ut sit hujus interni causa, quo alioqui careremus. Delectatur igitur Deus hoc interno peccato, quippe qui sine ulla necessitate libere nobis illud extra nos positum peccatum imputat, ut vi illius imputationis producatur internum illud in nobis peccatum, quod alioqui non posset produci. Hoccine est glorificare Deum, & non potius eum facere, (quod sine horrore conscientiae pronunciare non possum,) autorem peccati nostri?

choices.choice: Inherent desert enough; free extra-us imputation would make God author of sin
